recordedBy: Session C, Part C (lane CHECKS), from measurements taken by the integration owner on main this session
why: The close-out that produced 2026-08-31-41.json reported 14 of 14 gates green. The record it wrote in the same handoff says test FAIL. The record is the truthful artifact and the close-out sentence was not. A later session comparing the two would otherwise have to re-derive the reconciliation, and the two obvious readings of it are both wrong.

actualFromTheRecord.note: 13 of 14, not 14 of 14. Every other gate in that record — lint, tsc, governance:check, orchestration:check, method:check, control-plane:gate, feedback:sweep, assert:browser, db:gate, release:freeze, build, test:bundle, build:standalone — recorded PASS.

theMechanism.headline: A FALSE RED ON THE TEST GATE IS PRODUCIBLE ON DEMAND BY RUNNING IT UNDER CONCURRENT LOAD ON THIS HOST. It presents as an EARLY ABORT with no named failing test.
theMechanism.discriminatingFact: The failing run took 59s. A complete passing run of the same tree takes 75s. It failed FASTER than a full run takes, so it did not fail an assertion — it aborted before reaching the summary. A suite that fails an assertion runs to the end and reports `fail N`.
theMechanism.whyItWasNeverAttributable: There was never a named failing test to find. A session hunting one keeps coming up empty and eventually calls the suite flaky, which is the wrong conclusion and the reason this kept recurring.
measuredOnMain: pnpm gates on main ac3cfced plus the governance change: test gate FAIL in 59s, recorded at data/ops/gate-runs/2026-08-31-42.json.
pnpm test standalone, same tree, minutes later: EXIT 0 — tests 4274, suites 26, pass 4274, fail 0, cancelled 0, skipped 0, duration_ms 74582.
scripts/gates.mjs invokes the literal string `pnpm test`, byte-identical to the `test` script in package.json. Same command, same tree, opposite results.
theMechanism.load: Seven parallel worktree agents were running pnpm install, pnpm build and pnpm test concurrently on this Windows host. Gate record 41 (18d1f808, test FAIL) and record 37 (62f108e1, test FAIL) both landed during comparable parallel activity, while 38, 39 and 40 — interleaved between them at nearly the same SHAs — passed. THE TEST GATE IS NOT ISOLATED FROM CONCURRENT LOAD ON THE HOST. Under contention a child process dies and node --test exits non-zero with no assertion to report.
theMechanism.standingRule: A session that sees `test FAIL` with nothing attributable MUST re-run it ISOLATED before believing it. It may not ship on it, and it may not record it as green either.

whatTheFlakeProbeDoesAndDoesNotSay.says: 6 consecutive runs of the full suite, 4170 pass, 0 fail, 0 context rewrites, verdict NOT_REPRODUCED.
whatTheFlakeProbeDoesAndDoesNotSay.doesNotSay: It does NOT clear the tree record 41 was taken on. The probe counted 4170 passing tests; the same suite on main this session counts 4274. That is +104 tests, so the probe cleared a DIFFERENT TREE, roughly ten hours older than 18d1f808. It is corroborating evidence about the suite's general health and nothing more. Reading NOT_REPRODUCED as a clearance of 18d1f808 is the sharpest error available here.

notYetOnThisBranch: The integration owner's gate run on main — test FAIL in 59s, against the pnpm test that exits 0 on the same tree minutes later — is the measurement this correction rests on. Its record lands on main as a gate-run record of its own and is NOT cited above, because a correction may not cite a file that is not on disk beside it; tests/gate-run-corrections.test.ts refuses that, and refused it here. Read it as the record whose runId names the run described in theMechanism.measuredOnMain. It is evidence FOR this finding and must not be treated as a clean gate reading.
alsoKnown: A separate, real hazard sits nearby and is not this one: tests/tracker-transaction.test.ts writes a synthetic row into the LIVE tracker store and restores it in a finally, so a run killed mid-test leaves the row behind and the NEXT suite fails two tests for a reason that looks unrelated. That mechanism produces an ASSERTION failure with named failing tests. Record 41 was not that — it named nothing, and it was faster than a complete run.

guardAdded.what: Every gate result now records failureKind (ASSERTION_FAILURE / EARLY_ABORT / UNATTRIBUTED, derived from the suite's own printed summary rather than from the exit code), suiteTotals (tests / pass / fail when a summary was printed), and nodeProcessesAtStart (how busy the host was when the gate started, null when unknown, never zero).
guardAdded.why: A gate record that stores only {id, ciJob, command, status, seconds} cannot tell a real failure from a process killed by host contention, and naming the cause of record 41 cost a full suite re-run. An EARLY_ABORT now says so on the console and in the record, and says that it is not evidence about the tree.

howThisWasCorrected: FORWARD, not by rewriting. 2026-08-31-41.json is left exactly as the instrument wrote it — it is generated (RULING 92) and it was not the thing that lied. This file sits beside it, cites every record it rests on, and is validated against the record it corrects by tests/gate-run-corrections.test.ts, so a correction can never state a count the record does not actually contain.
